editorialNotes: This story begins with the author's personal observation of the same plants on different days: abundant yellow flowers in the earlier photograph and far fewer flowers in the later photograph.
Impermanence and dependent origination are related Buddhist concepts but should not be treated as identical.
Dependent origination is a broad and foundational Buddhist teaching and should not be attributed exclusively to the Lotus Sutra.
Any discussion of the Lotus Sutra must use a verified passage from an authoritative translation before attributing a specific teaching or quotation to that text.
The discussion of marriage is a personal reflection on relationships changing through many conditions. It is not presented as canonical Buddhist doctrine.
The phrase 'duyên vợ chồng' is used in its ordinary Vietnamese cultural and reflective sense and must not be treated as identical to the technical Buddhist doctrine of dependent origination.
The story must not suggest that difficulties in a marriage are simply the karma or fault of either spouse.

Quantum entanglement describes particular quantum systems with strongly correlated or shared quantum states. It does not mean that every particle in the universe is entangled with every other particle.
Quantum entanglement and Buddhist dependent origination are not equivalent concepts.
Quantum physics is not presented as scientific proof of Buddhism, and Buddhism is not presented as having predicted quantum mechanics.

A husband and wife are not described as physically quantum-entangled systems. Entanglement is used only as a carefully bounded scientific comparison that can inspire reflection about independence and relationship.
The comparison between Buddhism and quantum physics is philosophical and exploratory, not evidence that the two traditions describe the same phenomenon.
